ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, $AC=BC$, $BE\perp CE$ at $E$, and $AD\perp CE$ at $D$. We have $\triangle ADC \cong \triangle CEB$. Given $AD=5\text{cm}$ and $DE=3\text{cm}$, find the length of $BE$ in cm.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} \\
From (1), we know that $\triangle ADC \cong \triangle CEB$,\\
hence $AD = CE = 5\,\text{cm}$, and $CD = BE$.\\
Since $CD = CE - DE$,\\
it follows that $BE = AD - DE = 5 - 3 = \boxed{2}\,\text{cm}$.

From the diagram, take CE as an axis with C at coordinate 0, D at coordinate \(x\), and E at coordinate \(x+3\), because \(DE=3\) and D is between C and E.
